title: Trivial scalar condensed coefficients are acyclic for pro-prime-to-ell groups
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E,\Omega$, let $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ with all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Use a small coherent profinite site in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $K$ let $\mathcal A_K(C_F)$ be the category of internal $C_F$-modules with $C_F$-linear action of the condensed group $\underline K(S)=C(S,K)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and let $R\Gamma_K$ be the ordinary total right derived invariant-submodule functor [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Give the regular module $C_F$ the trivial $K$-action. If every finite continuous quotient of $K$ has order prime to $\ell$, the canonical augmentation
$$\eta_{K,F}:C_F[0]\longrightarrow R\Gamma_K(C_F[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$. Here $[0]$ places a module in cochain degree zero, and the augmentation is induced by the inclusion of invariant sections into an injective resolution, with $\Gamma_K(C_F)=C_F$. This concerns ordinary internal condensed modules and the noncomplete norm-topological $\Omega$, with no completion or restriction to locally constant functions.

proof.text: Fix $F=E$ or $\Omega$ and put $A=C_F$. By [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] with $G=K$ and trivial $N=A$, there is a normalized isomorphism $\theta:R\Gamma_K(A[0])\cong\mathscr B_F(K)$. Its degree-zero augmentation is invariant inclusion. Apply [lem-sfb-prime-to-ell-scalar-bar-model] for the same $K,F$: the canonical resolution comparison $j:Q(\mathcal C_F^\bullet(K))\to\mathscr B_F(K)$ is an isomorphism, and $jQ(u)$ is that augmentation. Thus $\theta\eta_{K,F}=jQ(u)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel input: old steps 1–2 and 6; normalized bar comparison.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-prime-to-ell-cochain-finite-quotient-descent]. Its quotient-order hypothesis is precisely ours, so its actual inclusion $\iota:\mathcal L_F^\bullet(K)\to\mathcal C_F^\bullet(K)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. In degree zero both are $A$ and $\iota^0=1_A$. By [lem-sfb-prime-to-ell-finite-quotient-sheaf-augmentation], $Q(u_L):A[0]\to Q(\mathcal L_F^\bullet(K))$ is an isomorphism. Since $u=\iota u_L$, we have $Q(u)=Q(\iota)Q(u_L)$, a composite of isomorphisms.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar tame-kernel input: old steps 3–5; finite-quotient comparison and local averaging.

proof.text: The equality from step 1 now gives $\eta_{K,F}=\theta^{-1}jQ(\iota)Q(u_L)$, so the specified augmentation is an isomorphism. The degree-zero identities and resolution augmentations ensure this is the canonical invariant inclusion, rather than an unspecified isomorphism between the objects. For $K=1$ the maps reduce to the identity and its canonical resolution comparison. Repeat for each of $F=E,\Omega$.
